# FIG. 1

A perspective view of a drilling jig on a workpiece 90.

The workpiece 90 is a flat panel, and one straight side of the panel is the workpiece edge 92.

A long straight rail 10 rests on the front face of the workpiece 90, spaced inward from the workpiece edge 92, well inside the drawing area. A fence 30 is attached to the left end of the rail 10 and crosses the rail 10 transverse to its length, reaching from the rail 10 toward the workpiece edge 92. A downwardly projecting portion 32 of the fence 30 depends alongside the longitudinal side of the rail 10 that faces the workpiece edge 92, extends below the rail 10, and contacts the workpiece edge 92.

Two guide carriages, a first guide carriage 50 and a second guide carriage 70, rest on top of the rail 10, the first guide carriage 50 nearer the fence 30 and the second guide carriage 70 farther from the fence 30. Each guide carriage is shown schematically as a plain block surmounted by a plain round body that represents the clamp knob of that guide carriage. No reference numeral is applied to either clamp knob on this sheet; the clamp knobs are numbered on FIG. 8 and FIG. 9.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 10: rail
- 30: fence
- 32: downwardly projecting portion
- 50: first guide carriage
- 70: second guide carriage
- 90: workpiece
- 92: workpiece edge

# FIG. 2

A top plan view of the drilling jig.

The long, straight rail 10 is seen from above and extends across the drawing area from left to right. A longitudinal slot 16 runs lengthwise along the rail 10 as a straight elongated opening, shown schematically.

Distance marks 18 are a row of short transverse graduation lines on the upper surface of the rail 10, along one long side of the longitudinal slot 16.

The fence 30 is at the left end of the rail 10 and is shown schematically as a plain rectangular body crossing the rail 10 transverse to its length.

The first guide carriage 50 and the second guide carriage 70 are two separate bodies, shown schematically as plain rectangular bodies, resting on top of the rail 10, the first guide carriage 50 nearer the fence 30 and the second guide carriage 70 farther from the fence 30. Each carriage overlaps and hides the part of the longitudinal slot 16 beneath it. On each carriage are drawn, without reference numerals on this sheet, the clamp knob seen from above, the circular opening of the drill bushing bore, and the short index line of the pointer ending beside the distance marks 18; these features are numbered on FIG. 8 and FIG. 9.

A broken, offset cutting-plane line 3-3 establishes the cross-sectional view of FIG. 3. It crosses the second guide carriage 70 transverse to the length of the rail 10, beginning clear of one long side of the rail 10 and ending clear of the other long side. The line is stepped, one transverse leg lying on the axis of the drill bushing bore of that carriage and the other on the axis of its clamp knob, the two joined by a short leg running lengthwise of the rail 10, so that the single section of FIG. 3 shows both that bore and that clamp knob with its shank and clamping shoe. The numeral 3 designates each of the two ends, and an arrow at each end points to the left, toward the fence 30.

A second broken, offset cutting-plane line 5-5 establishes the cross-sectional view of FIG. 5. It crosses the first guide carriage 50 in the same manner and is stepped in the same way about the axis of the drill bushing bore of that carriage and the axis of its clamp knob. The numeral 5 designates each of the two ends, and an arrow at each end points to the left, toward the fence 30.

## Numerals shown on this figure

- 10: rail
- 16: longitudinal slot
- 18: distance marks
- 30: fence
- 50: first guide carriage
- 70: second guide carriage
